nameStory: The Atlantic halibut gets its name from the old English words 'haly' (holy) and 'butte' (flatfish), meaning 'holy flatfish.' This name likely came about because halibut was traditionally eaten on Catholic holy days when meat was forbidden. The massive size of these fish made them a prized catch that could feed many people during religious observances.
description: The Atlantic halibut is a giant flatfish that lives on the ocean bottom, with both eyes positioned on its dark upper side. It's the world's largest flatfish, capable of growing up to 15 feet long and weighing over 700 pounds, though most caught today are much smaller. These powerful swimmers have a diamond-shaped body that's perfectly adapted for life on sandy and rocky sea floors. Atlantic halibut are incredibly long-lived fish that can reach 50 years old.

idTips.label: Body Shape
idTips.description: Distinctive diamond-shaped flatfish body that's much longer than it is wide, with a thick, muscular feel when handled - not thin and delicate like smaller flounders

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Dark brown to olive-green on the eyed side with lighter mottling, while the blind side is pure white - the contrast is striking when you flip the fish over

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Massive size potential - even young halibut are noticeably larger and heavier than other flatfish, with a solid, dense body that requires two hands to lift

idTips.label: Mouth
idTips.description: Large mouth with sharp teeth that extends past the eye, designed for grabbing fish and squid - much more aggressive-looking than smaller flatfish

idTips.label: Fins
idTips.description: Small eyes positioned on the right side of the head, with the top eye slightly forward of the bottom eye, and a straight lateral line

habitat: Atlantic halibut live on sandy, gravel, or clay bottoms in deep New England waters, typically found between 200 to 6,600 feet deep in the cold waters of the Gulf of Maine and Georges Bank. They prefer areas with strong currents where they can ambush prey from the bottom. These fish are most commonly encountered by deep-sea commercial fishermen rather than recreational anglers due to their preference for deep, offshore waters.

seasonality.spring: Halibut begin moving into slightly shallower waters as they prepare for summer feeding. This is when commercial fishermen have the best chance of encountering them.
seasonality.summer: Most active feeding period when halibut are in peak condition. They're found in their shallowest waters of the year, though still quite deep by most standards.
seasonality.fall: Halibut start moving to deeper wintering grounds. Their bodies are at maximum weight after the summer feeding season.
seasonality.winter: Found in their deepest waters of the year, becoming less active in the cold. Rarely encountered during this season.

funFact: Atlantic halibut start life swimming upright like normal fish, but as they grow, one eye literally migrates across their skull to join the other eye, and they tip over to live sideways on the bottom - it's like nature's own magic trick happening over several months!
confusionNotes: Young Atlantic halibut can be confused with other large flounders, but halibut have their eyes on the right side of their head while some similar species have eyes on the left side. Remember: halibut are 'right-eyed' fish, and even small ones feel noticeably thicker and more muscular than other flatfish of similar length.
contextualKnowledge: Atlantic halibut populations have been severely depleted by overfishing, making them quite rare in New England waters today compared to historical abundance. What was once a common fish that fed coastal communities for generations is now a protected species that most people will never see in person.
compareHints: Atlantic halibut is the only species in its genus found in New England waters, making it unique among local flatfish. Compared to other large flounders in the righteye flounder family, halibut are distinguished by their massive potential size, right-eyed orientation, and much more robust, muscular body build. While other flounders max out at a few pounds, halibut can weigh hundreds of pounds and have a distinctly powerful, thick-bodied appearance.
